chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about tayammum, and he said: Two times, two times for the face and the hands.

So the way to reconcile these reports is that what they contain regarding one strike is to be specified for minor ritual purity, and what they contain regarding two strikes is for major ritual purity, so that the reports do not contradict one another. And that which indicates this distinction is:

key_terms.مَرَّتَيْنِ: two times; here referring to the number of strikes
key_terms.ٱلتَّفْصِيلِ: the distinction or detailed differentiation between the cases
key_terms.ٱلتَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum, the dry ablution performed in place of wudu or ghusl
key_terms.ٱلضَّرْبَةِ ٱلْوَاحِدَةِ: one strike upon the earth or dust
key_terms.ٱلطَّهَارَةِ ٱلصُّغْرَىٰ: minor ritual purity, associated with wudu (ablution)
key_terms.ٱلطَّهَارَةِ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ: major ritual purity, associated with ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.ٱلْوَجْهِ: the face, one of the areas wiped in tayammum
key_terms.ٱلْيَدَيْنِ: the two hands, wiped in tayammum

ai.seo_question: How are the narrations about one strike and two strikes in tayammum reconciled?
ai.summary: This report discusses the number of strikes in tayammum and states that it is done two times for the face and the hands. The closing editorial note reconciles differing reports by assigning one strike to minor ritual impurity and two strikes to major ritual impurity.
